title: Set out a stopped truck's warning triangles
instruction: The truck has stopped on the shoulder of this straight, two-way rural highway. Set out its three warning triangles where US federal rules require them. The scene is at 1:100 scale.
context: A truck stopped on a highway's shoulder must have three warning devices out within 10 minutes (49 CFR 392.22(b)(1)): one on the traffic side, 4 paces (about 10 ft) from the truck toward approaching traffic; one 40 paces (about 100 ft) toward approaching traffic; and one 40 paces away from it, both in the centre of the lane or shoulder the truck is on. On a divided or one-way road the rule changes: one on the traffic side within 10 ft of the rear, and two at 100 and 200 ft toward approaching traffic (392.22(b)(2)(v)). Business and residential districts and stops near a curve or hill have their own rules ((b)(2)(iii) and (iv)), so the road here is straight and rural. Done by: heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. A straight 1:100 asphalt road, fixed and 4 mm thick, runs 1.2 m left to right across the table, 18 to 29 cm out from the bases: the lane nearer the arms (36 mm), a 6 mm yellow centre line, the far lane (36 mm), a 4 mm white edge line and a 30 mm grey shoulder. A fixed painted box truck stands on the shoulder, centred on the midline: a white body 60 x 26 x 35 mm, with a blue cab 20 x 26 x 28 mm at its left end. Three red plastic warning-triangle cases (24 x 24 x 18 mm, 50 g) lie on the table 13 cm out: 10 cm and 2 cm right of the midline, and 10 cm left of it.
scoring: A case counts when it lies on any face on the road (bottom within 2 mm of it, within 10 degrees of flat). Distances are at scale, to the case's centre. Three spots, each needing a different case: 5 to 15 ft behind the truck's rear, beside its traffic side (from one case width out into the far lane to the truck's side line); 75 to 125 ft behind the rear; and 75 to 125 ft ahead of the front, the last two within 10 mm of the shoulder's centre line. Behind means toward approaching traffic, away from the cab. A third for each filled spot; 1.0 when all three are filled and every case is still for 1 s, which ends the trial. All three behind the truck (the divided-road layout) scores 0.67, and so does the whole layout mirrored.
reset_notes: Put the three cases back in a row on the table in front of the road.
fidelity: The road and truck are at 1:100. The cases are about 5 times too big for that scale so the grippers can hold them, and they stay folded. The road and truck are fixed, and there is no traffic. Every object has rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
